newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BANKRUPT WILLEM SOPHIA SURGES ON BRUSSELS BOURSE.
newsitem.headline: BANKRUPT WILLEM SOPHIA SURGES ON BRUSSELS BOURSE.

text.p: Shares in Belgian coal mine SA des Charbonnages Neerlandais Willem Sophia , in liquidation since 1973, surged on the Brussels bourse on Monday after liquidators announced a windfall payment to shareholders.
Willem Sophia rose more than threefold to 4,555 francs from 1,400 francs with some 240 shares traded. The stock trades on Brussels' secondary market where prices are fixed once a day.
In a notice published in Belgian newspapers on Saturday liquidators said shareholders would in September receive around 4,700 Belgian francs per share and the company would then be delisted.

Willem Sophia, founded in 1898, is one of several former coal mines that although bankrupt are still listed because they stand to benefit from funds set aside to cover the cost of clearing up environmental and other damages. Many of the mines also owned property which has gradually been sold off.
Willem Sophia last paid a dividend in 1991. Its biggest shareholder is Societe des Participations Industrielles, a privately-held investment vehicle of Belgium's Boel family.
